A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original TCA classification results, component and hyperparameter ablations, and visual analyses, including appendix experiments with ViT-L/14 and ImageNet distribution shifts.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds CIFAR-100-C corruption results and evaluations using SigLIP and SigLIP v2.

M1.justification: v3 adapts TCA to SigLIP models by using pooled features and attention weights for domain anchors, token scoring, and logits correction instead of CLIP's visual class tokens (Sections 3.2 and 4.1). The existing CLIP reservoir, pruning, coreset merging, and correction procedures remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR-100-C classification under contrast, snow, and brightness corruptions, introducing controlled image degradation beyond the previously evaluated distribution shifts. The ten cross-dataset benchmarks and ImageNet/ImageNet-A/V2/R/S coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Unadapted SigLIP and SigLIP v2 inference become additional reference systems in v3 Table 3. Comparator membership in the retained CLIP experiments is unchanged, including the TDA-plus-token-condensation comparison. The new corruption experiment reuses CLIP and EViT.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a systematic five-severity evaluation for each of three corruptions and experiments using SigLIP and SigLIP v2 with ViT-B/16 at R = 0.9. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Existing CLIP batch size, augmentation policy, backbones, and retention settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 2 tests whether TCA withstands progressively stronger image corruptions compared with ordinary inference and EViT. This adds a substantial controlled robustness analysis. Existing component, reservoir, computational-budget, and hyperparameter analyses are retained; moving the TDA comparison and correction-parameter ablations does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the empirical results. v3's added experiments retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice; its theoretical bound does not introduce empirical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for 15 corruption/severity conditions and both SigLIP models. Table 3 reports average gains of 2.21% and 1.32% over SigLIP and SigLIP v2 inference, respectively, with small Food101 declines. All nine corresponding v2 tables retain their numerical values, including TCA's 68.69% accuracy at 15.45 GFLOPs in Table 1.

T1.justification: New appendix Section 5.2 models token selection through a Gibbs posterior and states a generalization bound involving KL divergence, introducing a formal framework absent from v2. It explicitly provides no rigorous proof. The existing K-center objective and merging equations are relocated to Section 5.1, rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden TCA from a CLIP-specific contribution to adaptation across VLMs, explicitly including SigLIP, SigLIP v2, and corruption robustness. The conclusion also introduces theoretical analysis as supporting material. The training-free efficiency claim and maximum reported 21.4% improvement are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of corruption robustness and an unproved explanation involving reduced KL divergence. New Section 5.6 ties applicability to cross-modal alignment and explains why direct application to LLaVA is problematic. Existing severe-shift limitations remain, while v2's suggestion to estimate adaptive condensation rates from merging-center distances disappears.

D1.justification: v3 documents the SigLIP pooling adaptation and identifies CLIP ViT-B/16 as the default ablation model. It removes v2's abstract code hyperlink and introduction statement about supplementary source code. This establishes removal of access information, without establishing that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for common-corruption benchmarking, SigLIP, SigLIP 2, LLaVA, and studies of CLIP generalization through train-test similarity and spurious features. These support localized extensions in positioning; the main survey of TTA and token-condensation methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and much of the introduction are rewritten. The method is reorganized into overview, reservoir, token reduction, and logits-correction subsections, with coreset details moved to the appendix. Correction-parameter discussions move to the appendix, the TDA comparison moves into the main text, and domain-anchor terminology replaces domain class-token terminology throughout.

P2.justification: v3 adds two result tables, relocates the correction-parameter tables and TDA comparison chart, and updates diagram labels, captions, and Table 1 performance bolding. Existing plotted data, qualitative image panels, and the overall two-column visual format are preserved.

improvement.justification: The corruption tests and SigLIP evaluations add useful evidence about robustness and transfer beyond v2's CLIP study, while the reorganized method and applicability discussion improve clarity. These benefits provide a limited net improvement: the new theoretical bound remains underspecified and unproved, and removal of the code-access disclosure weakens reproducibility guidance.
